```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This example treats each sample as a multidimensional observation vector rather than a mesh vertex.

```{r}
library(fmapsR)
set.seed(123)

make_multidomain <- function(seed, n = 30, p = 12, k = 8) {
  set.seed(seed)
  X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)

  # Choose either covariance or kNN-laplacian operator families.
  operator <- fm_operator(X, method = "knn_laplacian", k = 7)

  fm_basis(
    fm_domain_generic(n_samples = n, data = X, operator = operator),
    k = k,
    solver = "base",
    cache = FALSE
  )
}

A <- make_multidomain(1)
B <- make_multidomain(2)

# Validation checks for non-shape operators
stopifnot(
  all(dim(A$operator) == c(A$n_samples, A$n_samples)),
  max(abs(A$operator - t(A$operator))) < 1e-8
)

desc_A <- A$data
desc_B <- B$data

fit <- fm_match(A, B, descriptors = list(source = desc_A, target = desc_B), penalties = list(descr = 1, lap = 1e-3, comm = 0.2), optimizer = "cg", cg_maxit = 6)
fit <- fm_refine(fit, method = "icp", nit = 3)

feature_A <- A$data[, 1]
feature_B_hat <- fm_transfer(fit, feature_A)

c(transfer_mse = mean((feature_B_hat - B$data[, 1])^2), p2p_cardinality = length(as_p2p(fit)))
```

## Takeaway

The API does not assume shapes. As long as you define:

1. Sample-wise descriptors (`n_samples x p`).
2. A basis-friendly operator (`n_samples x n_samples`).

you can run the full functional map pipeline.
